spans.s:
Kairāta is the name of a snake in the Atharvaveda--possibly, but not probably, the modern Karait.
Foot notes v. 13, 5. Cf. Whitney, Translation of the Atharvaveda, 243
Kairātikā, a ‘maiden of the kirāta people,’ is mentioned in the Atharvaveda (x. 4, 14) as digging up roots for medicinal use.
Kairiśi, ‘descendant of Kiriśa,’ is the patronymic of Sutvan in the aitareya brāhmaṇa (viii. 28).
